sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in an older postoperative patient demonstrates a rounded complex fluid collection with gas bubbles and an enhancing capsule , findings diagnostic for an abdominal abscess.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-01

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in an older postoperative patient demonstrates multiple loculated fluid collections with prominently enhancing capsules and mass effect on adjacent structures, representing abdominal abscesses. Note the air-fluid level within one of the abscesses.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-02

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows a large pelvic abscess following a hysterectomy. Note the presence of a discrete enhancing rim and mass effect on adjacent loops of bowel and the bladder.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-03

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows placement of a percutaneous drainage catheter using a transgluteal approach. The abscess has almost completely resolved following drainage.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-04

sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-05

sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-06

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT after ERCP shows a large collection of gas and fluid dissecting through the retroperitoneal spaces, especially the anterior pararenal space and the interfascial plane . These findings were due to perforation of the duodenum at the papillotomy site.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-07

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT demonstrates a large cystic mass with internal complexity. The mass was thought to represent an abscess and underwent unsuccessful drainage but was ultimately found to represent a gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST).
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-08

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Ultrasound demonstrates a complex cystic mass with internal septations and multiple areas of higher echogenicity located in the right adnexa, representing a large tuboovarian abscess in this patient with pelvic inflammatory disease (PID).
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-09

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T1 C+ FS MR demonstrates a rim-enhancing abscess in the right psoas muscle. Note the phlegmonous change and enhancement around the margins of the abscess, partially attributable to inflammation from the patient's Crohn disease.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-10

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT demonstrates a loculated fluid collection with prominent rim enhancement and surrounding soft tissue edema in the right lower quadrant, compatible with an abscess. sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-01

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows placement of a percutaneous drainage catheter into the abscess with a significant decrease in the size of the abscess following drainage.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-02

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in a patient with pelvic pain and fever demonstrates a thick-walled enhancing fluid collection abutting the adjacent inflamed sigmoid colon , representing a peridiverticular abscess related to perforated diverticulitis.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-03

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT demonstrates a peripherally enhancing "fluid collection" abutting the left colon and small bowel. This was thought to be an abscess and even underwent unsuccessful drainage, but was ultimately found to represent a gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST).
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-04

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T1 C+ FS MR in a young female patient in septic shock demonstrates thick-walled, peripherally enhancing fluid collections in the pelvis, compatible with abscesses.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-05

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Sagittal T2 MR in the same patient demonstrates the more anterior fluid collection is directly contiguous with the patient's C-section scar , compatible with uterine rupture as the cause for these abscesses. sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-06

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT demonstrates a large, rim-enhancing abscess in the perineum secondary to traumatic Foley catheter placement and urethral perforation.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-07

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT demonstrates a large, loculated fluid collection in the lesser sac with rim-enhancement and internal gas , representing an abscess with gas-forming infection. This infected collection was secondary to necrotizing pancreatitis.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-08

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Transverse color Doppler US in a young female patient with pelvic pain and fever demonstrates a complex cystic adnexal mass without substantial color flow vascularity.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-09

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in the same patient demonstrates a large fluid collection with rim enhancement and surrounding fat stranding (corresponding to the US finding), ultimately found to represent a tuboovarian abscess. Notice how the complexity in this collection is much more evident on US compared to CT.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-10

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in the same patient shows ectopic gas bubbles within abscess in pelvis .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-12

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT of gas-forming retrocecal abscess from perforated diverticulum. Note ectopic gas collection from posterior to cecum , cecal thickening, and adjacent fat stranding .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-13

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Transverse transabdominal US of a postoperative abscess found on a grayscale image is shown. Note the hypoechoic fluid collection with fluid-fluid level .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-14

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows intramural abscess of the sigmoid from diverticulitis. Note the long segment of the markedly thickened sigmoid and an ill-defined adjacent fluid collection .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-15

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in the same patient shows more discreet abscess collections on a lower plane of the section .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-16

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows pyogenic postoperative abscess after bowel resection. Note multiple fluid collections with enhancing rims. Gas is noted in pelvic abscess but not in other collections.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-18

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT demonstrates a gas-forming pyogenic liver abscess in a diabetic patient. Note air-fluid level within the abscess cavity .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-19

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial US shows a liver abscess demonstrating linear high-amplitude echoes with "dirty" distal acoustic shadowing representing gas .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-20

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows an amebic abscess. Note peripheral low-attenuation zone of edema surrounding the abscess.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-21

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Sagittal US shows amebic abscess. Note low-level echoes within the hypoechoic mass, and the lack of distal acoustic enhancement.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-22

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Sagittal US shows fungal microabscesses due to systemic candidiasis. Note multiple target lesions .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-23

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Sagittal US of the spleen demonstrates an abscess with low-level echoes .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-24

CORE_EVIDENCE_FILE_BEGIN
CORE_EVIDENCE_STATUS: USED
CORE_SOURCE_BASIS: junzi-shi-core-radiology-a-visual-approach-to.pdf; Gastrointestinal Imaging, including hepatic infection/pyogenic abscess pp. 116-118, pancreatitis complications pp. 150-151, splenic infection pp. 167-168, Crohn disease complications pp. 205-207, appendicitis pp. 210-211, diverticulitis pp. 218-219; Interventional Radiology drainage material including pp. 648-649.
CORE_FACTS_USED:

* Hepatic pyogenic abscess may arise from bowel processes including diverticulitis, appendicitis, Crohn disease, and bowel surgery; E. coli is the most common causative organism in that Core section.
* Hepatic abscess may mimic metastasis as a ring-enhancing mass; MRI may show central T2 hyperintensity and restricted diffusion; ultrasound can evolve from ill-defined phlegmon to a well-defined hypoechoic collection with internal echoes.
* Appendicitis can progress to gangrenous/perforated appendicitis with abscess; periappendicular abscess is a secondary ultrasound finding.
* Crohn disease may be complicated by abscess and fistula formation.
* Diverticulitis is complicated when abscess is present, and abscesses may undergo percutaneous drainage.
* Pancreatitis-related collections may become infected; gas suggests infection but absence of gas does not exclude it.
* Splenic bacterial abscesses may have an irregular enhancing wall; gas is highly specific when present. Fungal splenic abscesses are typically small, multiple, and occur in immunocompromised patients.
* Core IR material was used to cross-check drainage-related concepts and catheter management.
CORE_DERIVED_CARDS:
* PRIMARY UNKNOWN cards involving hepatic, splenic, appendiceal, Crohn-related, diverticular, and pancreatitis-related abscesses.
* Mechanism cards for perforated appendicitis and diverticulitis progressing to localized abscess.
* Epidemiology card testing E. coli as the most common organism in Core's hepatic pyogenic abscess section.
* High-Yield CT/MRI/ultrasound and drainage cards, plus the shared Core + RadPrimer + STATdx summary field.
CORE_LIMITATIONS:
* Core Radiology does not present a single dedicated general "Abdominal Abscess" entity section matching the fused RadPrimer/STATdx article; relevant Core coverage is distributed across multiple GI and IR subsections.
* RadPrimer/STATdx supplied the general abdominal-abscess definition, broad multimodality framework, detailed drainage thresholds, approximately 80% drainage success statement, and several specific mimic/case details not stated as a unified framework in Core.
CORE_EVIDENCE_FILE_END
